groups.display_name: Mansukhani family (Man Industries): Ramesh Chandra (R C) Mansukhani

founder.name: Mansukhani brothers, Rameshchandra (R C) and Jagdishchandra Jhamaklal (J C) Mansukhani

groups.control_summary: R C Mansukhani's line controls Man Industries: R C 15.0%, Nikhil 4.8%, daughter Heena Kalantri 6.5%, Man Finance Pvt Ltd 12.0% and others (FY26). J C Mansukhani's line now holds about 0.03% after the 2013 split.
groups.background: The Mansukhani family started the Man group in the 1970s. Man Industries was incorporated in 1988 to make aluminium extrusions and moved into submerged-arc welded (SAW) line pipes in 1995, becoming one of India's largest SAW pipe makers, with plants at Anjar (Gujarat) and Pithampur (Madhya Pradesh). A dispute between brothers R C and J C Mansukhani was settled in 2013 by dividing the businesses: R C kept Man Industries and J C took the demerged real estate arm, Man Infraprojects. In 2024 the company bought National Pipe Company, Saudi Arabia, for about USD 102 million. A SEBI order of September 2025 penalised the company, R C and Nikhil Mansukhani over alleged diversion of funds.

groups.background: P K Khurana incorporated Everest Kanto Cylinder in June 1978, initially jointly with the Thakkar family, who withdrew in 1983 (reported). It became India's largest maker of high-pressure seamless gas cylinders for industrial gases and CNG, with plants at Tarapur (Maharashtra) and Kandla (Gujarat) and overseas units in Dubai and the USA (CP Industries). After P K Khurana stepped down in 2019 and later died, his sons Pushkar and Puneet took over. CARE noted allegations by a former CFO in 2019.

groups.control_summary: Holding company J B Advani and Co Pvt Ltd owns 45.2% of Ador Welding (FY26; 50.0% in FY19); the founding families hold J B Advani and Co. The annual report says no two directors are related as defined by law.
groups.background: The group traces to a trading firm, J B Advani and Co, set up in Karachi in 1908 by five partners from the Advani, Malkani and Mirchandani families. In 1951 J B Advani and Co and Switzerland's Oerlikon-Buhrle set up Advani-Oerlikon, India's first maker of welding electrodes and equipment, which listed in 1986 and was renamed Ador Welding in 2003. The group also has Ador Fontech, Ador Powertron and consumer businesses. It is run by the fourth generation of the founding families: Ninotchka Malkani Nagpal chairs, Aditya Malkani is MD; Aruna B Advani was Executive Chairman in 2019.
